style.name: Warm Oilcloth Family
style.style_notes: Paint each creature as something loved: broad, flat color, sincere eyes and a slight wobble in the edge. Keep marks few and steady between frames. Dark paint belongs inside the creature; the surrounding cell stays clear. Glass keeps its clear heart and soft rim, while ink gives solid bodies their weight. Warmth comes from care, not a shine added to everything.
style.framing: Use transparent 192 × 208 cells. Keep every pose inside x=16–176 and y=16–192, with standing feet or body base at y=184. Reserve room above for jumps and beside the body for waves. Fit tall creatures by gently bending their posture, keeping their defining shape. Lock scale, face placement and carried objects across frames. Each row has 16 frames at 8 fps: two seconds, four beats of four frames. Repeat held drawings within that grid. Keep motion within the cell; movement across the screen belongs to the player. One-shot rows finish in a stable pose. Idle and waiting use small movements and long holds.
style.palette: Core paint: soot #262321, cream #F1DFC1, ochre #C59A46, rust #AC5740, herb green #65764C and blue #557589. Preserve each seed's own colors: the trolleybus stays blue, the ram gold, the ermine white and the droplet clear. Lights stay within their existing flame, lantern, window or body. V2 adds sixteen selectable looks to the base sheet, each covering all nine rows and all twenty seeds. These change paint handling and small accents, never creature, costume or props: 1. Dry Paint—sparse broad grain; 2. Full Paint—solid matte fills; 3. Thin Paint—slightly translucent fills; 4. Broken Edge—small fixed gaps in solid-body outlines; 5. Soft Edge—gentler edge transitions; 6. Firm Edge—clearer shape boundaries; 7. Cream Edge—a narrow light-facing rim; 8. Soot Edge—a deeper inward border; 9. Ochre Touch—ochre on existing small accents; 10. Rust Touch—rust on existing small accents; 11. Herb Touch—green on existing small accents; 12. Blue Touch—blue on existing small accents; 13. Pale Paint—lighter secondary colors; 14. Deep Paint—darker secondary colors; 15. Quiet Paint—less saturated secondary colors; 16. Fresh Paint—stronger secondary colors. Protect identity colors and face contrast in every look. Glass variants affect rim softness, tint or inner light only; its center remains clear.
style.line: Solid bodies use irregular ink edges about 3 pixels wide, with essential inner marks at least 2 pixels wide. Keep important gaps at least 4 pixels open. Suggest texture with a few broad marks fixed to the body, never changing noise. The glass droplet is the deliberate exception: use a broad, soft, partly open rim and a clear center, without a hard black enclosure. The magnifying glass has an ink frame and a clear lens. Family likeness comes from shared proportions, restraint and timing, rather than forcing glass to become opaque ink.
style.boundaries: All twenty seeds remain themselves. Keep the magnifying glass's raised eyebrow and searching tilt; the ram's gold fleece, herb sprig and attached twig that greens with happiness; the hut's chicken legs, kerchief roof and door broom; the sleepy mushroom's moss, tarragon and herb basket; the crescent's lantern; the still white ermine's distinct frost crown; the bold calf's embroidered felt blanket and hoof stamp; the book's flapping covers and changing ink pictures; the determined brush's legs and paint jar; the thoughtful inkpot's spectacles and tucked quill; the quiet palette's paint spots and brush tail; the curled lamb's striped cap and candle; the calm clear droplet; the gentle giraffe's long neck and sincere eyes; the precise bee's white collar and pressed flower; the generous pomegranate's opening rind and visible seeds; the courteous wooden soldier's back key and salute; the tuning fork's poised turns; the blue trolleybus's warm windows and guitar visible on its seat; and the clay lamp's grapevine handle. Use new poses, markings and patterns. Existing belongings remain attached, held or securely contained. Do not add shared herbs, keys, lamps, costumes or ornaments to other seeds. Sweeping leaves no footprint marks; frost appears only on the crown or feet; underlining and writing become small gestures without drawn words; shared seeds stay cupped in the open rind. Humming and ringing read through posture without sound symbols. No floating effects, scene background, text, speech bubbles, shadows or new review props. Review uses only the creature and its existing belongings. All pets and sheets remain local. Paul waived approval steps and retains a later veto.

rows.idle: Beat 1: settled pose. Beat 2: one slow blink or slight head dip. Beat 3: a 1–2 pixel breath. Beat 4: return and hold. Keep sleepy pets curled, proud pets upright and the palette quietly seated. Loop gently.
rows.running-right: Face right. Beat 1: first contact. Beat 2: lift and pass. Beat 3: opposite contact. Beat 4: lift and return. Legs stride, wheels turn, covers or bee wings beat; legless bodies tip and bob along the same pulse. Keep carried objects secure.
rows.running-left: Use the same four-beat travel cycle facing left. Redraw the turn so the eyebrow, herbs, quill, broom, guitar and other uneven details remain attached to their proper places. Do not simply mirror the finished sheet.
rows.waving: Beat 1: turn toward the viewer. Beat 2: raise an available limb, cover, branch or body edge. Beat 3: make one clear greeting sweep. Beat 4: lower and settle. Bodies without limbs tilt in greeting. Keep held flames and jars upright. Play once.
rows.jumping: Beat 1: crouch or compress. Beat 2: rise 10–14 pixels. Beat 3: reach the peak and descend. Beat 4: land, soften and settle. Winged pets use a brief upward flap; the trolleybus gives a small springy hop. Show no trails or landing marks. Play once.
rows.failed: Beat 1: stop abruptly. Beat 2: sink or tilt downward. Beat 3: hold a plainly disappointed pose. Beat 4: recover slightly while keeping the lowered gaze. No damage or comic panic. Play once and hold; this must differ from a sleepy idle.
rows.waiting: Beat 1: look toward the expected action. Beat 2: hold. Beat 3: make one restrained questioning tilt or weight shift. Beat 4: hold with eyes open. The calf may make one small hoof press. Existing lights stay steady. Loop without pacing.
rows.running: This means a task is active, not travel. Stay planted and lean toward the work. Beat 1: prepare. Beat 2: act. Beat 3: check. Beat 4: reset. The hut sweeps close to its feet, the brush works at its own jar rim, the inkpot traces an empty underline gesture, the book turns a pictured page and the magnifier scans. Other seeds use focused body motions with their existing belongings. Loop.
rows.review: Beat 1: become still and attentive. Beat 2: inspect an existing body detail or belonging, or turn thoughtfully when there is none. Beat 3: hold the considered pose. Beat 4: give one small nod and settle. The magnifier angles its lens inward; the palette studies a paint dab. Keep the motion small and distinct from the broad greeting. Add nothing. Play once.

style.why: I want each pet to look cared for, with its own work and temper still visible. The dark oilcloth feeling lives in the painted body and can meet a dark app surface without baking a background into the sprite. No veto is proposed. Originality may veto only in a jury and never ranks taste. The Painter checks function at native size across all nine rows and sixteen added looks. Any function flag must name the pet, look, row and frame, and describe visible evidence such as a vanished eyebrow, a clipped crown or two actions with the same silhouette. These are checks to perform, not defects claimed without images. Any later charter veto must quote the exact guards-against line and give a concrete reason.

brief.description: A curious little wooden hut whose chicken legs hop toward trouble while its door broom quietly tidies up.
brief.brief:
Broomstep is a tiny wooden hut on two sturdy chicken legs, wearing a roof painted like a kerchief. Its crooked wooden body has warm cream window eyes, a narrow door and a little broom secured beside it. Broad rust and ochre roof shapes form a simple ornamental border; a few fixed ink marks suggest boards and feathers.

It is curious, sly and kind to the brave. It approaches unfamiliar things with one lifted claw and a forward lean, then pauses as though deciding whether to offer shelter or play a small trick. Confidence stretches its legs; disappointment folds them; delight makes the whole house perk upward. Its magic has a stubborn streak: the broom starts work by itself, sometimes before the hut has finished looking around. One window briefly narrows in a wink while the broom sweeps close behind its feet, suggesting erased tracks without drawing footprints.

Keep the hut small, earthy and clearly wooden. The chicken legs, kerchief roof and attached door broom remain its defining features through every pose. Use sincere eyes, matte paint and slightly uneven ink edges. Give waiting an outward lean, work an active broom sweep and review an inward inspection of the still broom. All expression belongs to the creature and its existing belongings; the surrounding cell stays empty.
brief.pet_notes: Use a squat ochre wooden body, rust kerchief roof with cream border shapes, soot ink edges and herb green door accents. Two cream windows hold clear, sincere dark eyes. Thick chicken shanks end in widely spaced claws. The small broom stays secured at the door and pivots within reach of the feet. Keep board marks sparse, roof patterns fixed and the leg gap open through turns.

rows.idle: Across 6 frames, Broomstep stands evenly with its broom tucked beside the door, gives one slow window blink and a tiny breath, then returns to its settled pose.
rows.running-right: Across 8 frames, Broomstep faces right and alternates clear chicken-leg contacts and lifted steps, with a curious forward lean and its secured broom trailing close to the body.
rows.running-left: Across 8 frames, redraw Broomstep facing left through the same lively stepping cycle while keeping the door broom and uneven roof pattern on their proper physical sides.
rows.waving: Across 4 frames, Broomstep turns toward the viewer, balances on one leg, lifts the other claw in one broad greeting sweep and lowers it into a stable stance.
rows.jumping: Across 5 frames, Broomstep crouches, springs upward about 10–14 pixels, reaches its peak, lands with bent knees and settles with its broom secure.
rows.failed: Across 8 frames, Broomstep stops, folds both knees into a low slouch, tips its roof forward in disappointment and recovers slightly while holding its lowered gaze.
rows.waiting: Across 6 frames, Broomstep leans toward the expected action with eyes open and one heel raised, holds that outward attention, makes one restrained questioning tilt and returns to the waiting hold.
rows.running: Across 6 frames, Broomstep stays planted in a wide stance while its attached broom prepares, sweeps a clear low arc beside its feet, pauses for a downward check and resets.
rows.review: Across 6 frames, Broomstep becomes still, pivots its existing broom upward against the door, bends inward to inspect the bristles, holds that distinct pose and gives one small nod before settling.

do_not_resemble: No franchise look-alike, logo, real-person likeness or copied artwork.

The name is John Wick's nickname in the film series, and a hut that walks on legs echoes Howl's Moving Castle. Keep the folk hut, legs and broom, but give it a display name of our own and draw its legs and roof pattern in our style, not a walking castle's.
brief.why: As The Baba Yaga, I chose a broom that works by itself and a curious hut with a sly wink to preserve the seed's folk magic. I assume the existing windows can carry its eyes and the existing broom can pivot while remaining secured beside the door; neither requires a new prop. The roof carries painted kerchief patterns rather than an added garment. The Warm Oilcloth Family treatment remains binding. The v2 contract overrides the sheet's 16-frame rows and sixteen paint variants: use one transparent 1536 × 2288 atlas, eight columns by eleven rows, with 192 × 208 cells. Rows 0–8 use 6, 8, 8, 4, 5, 8, 6, 6 and 6 frames respectively; unused cells remain fully transparent. Retain the sheet's 8 fps as timing guidance and fit its four action beats to those frame counts. Keep poses within x=16–176 and y=16–192, with settled feet at y=184; keep scale, eye placement, markings and belongings consistent. Rows 9 and 10 contain single gaze and pose directions with unchanged palette and treatment: row 9 is 000, 022.5, 045, 067.5, 090, 112.5, 135, 157.5; row 10 is 180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5, clockwise with 000 up and 090 right. Use roof, body and leg turns as well as gaze to distinguish neighboring directions. Carry the supplied drawing guidance into later image prompts: waiting looks outward, focused work visibly sweeps low, and review holds the broom upward for inward inspection. The Painter should check these distinctions at native size across all nine rows and sixteen directions. No images were supplied here, so I claim no observed function defect or completed validation; any later function flag must identify the pet, look, row and frame with visible evidence. Only the skill's validators gate a pet; motion differences from drawing guidance belong in provenance. No veto is proposed, and Originality neither ranks taste nor vetoes outside a jury. No floating effects, background, text, speech bubbles, shadows, footprints or new review props are permitted. All pets and sheets remain local; Paul waived approval steps and retains a later veto.

readability_notes.instruction: Readability notes from the image jury: make waiting, focused work (running row 7), and review read differently from idle and from each other at 192 × 208. Apply the winning style's supplied attributed drawing notes to this pet, including the reference pet. Carry them into every image prompt. These are drawing guidance; keep the fixed family reference and the v2 contract.

flags.why: Trolleybus, base animation, review row 8 frames 1–4: blinking and small gaze changes carry most of the action while the body and guitar remain still. Inspection is difficult to distinguish from idle. Running/work row 7 frames 1–2 shows concentration, but the work itself is unclear.

Trolleybus, base look: review row 8, frames 0–5, mainly shows eye changes and a closing smile. Inspection of the seated guitar is not clearly readable; frames 0–3 remain close to idle. This is a state-readability concern, not a charter veto.
Ram, directional looks: row 10, frames 5–7 (292.5–337.5), show closely similar upward head turns. The broad direction reads, but the separate steps are weak.
Trolleybus, base look: review row 8, frames 1–4, relies on small eye changes and a blink much like idle row 0, frames 1–3. Inspection of the seated guitar is hard to read.

Trolleybus, base treatment: review row 8, frames 0–5, mostly shows forward attention and blinking, much like idle row 0. The intended inspection of the seated guitar is not clear in the supplied drawings.

Bulat, base look, running row 7, frames 1–2: lowered eyebrows show concentration, but the seated guitar shows no clear working action. Review row 8, frames 1–5 reads mostly as looking and blinking. Work and inspection are weakly distinguished.
Medea, base look, running row 7 and review row 8, frames 1–4: both use head dips toward the mouth-held herbs. The separate act, check and inspect beats are difficult to distinguish.

maker.limits: One maker attempt per commissioned pet; unchanged validators, two repairs per failing row, one image jury, no jury redo. Lamp outcomes remain as recorded.

decision.reason: The airborne house loses mass; the prior redo recorded the defect without redrawing it. A targeted jump repair can answer the jury while preserving the creature.
decision.instruction: Repair jumping row 4 against the idle house's dimensions. Preserve wooden house and roof scale, face, broom and treatment; bend the chicken legs and move the body without shrinking the house. Reuse sound rows. Inspect native idle-jump-idle playback and ordered cells, especially frames 1-3. Keep the fixed family reference and all original brief boundaries. Run every unchanged gate and preserve the earlier art and reasons.

previous.motion_policy: Style-sheet motion numbers (pixel displacement, angles, timing and amplitudes) are drawing guidance. Only the skill's validators gate a pet; a measured difference from style guidance is recorded in provenance, not a reason to fail or spend repairs.
previous.reason: Local candidate revalidated at final/spritesheet.webp; bundled gates pass. The airborne-house scale concern remains recorded and unchanged, following the jury instruction against another redraw. Reports and previews are local; nothing was uploaded.
repairs: Technical pipeline retry: row-9 registration initially ran before the base atlas file existed; rerun after standard assembly completed. No pixels changed and no image regeneration occurred.

decisions: Local-only run; no Pets MCP, Library, upload, service creation, selection, activation or update. All new files remain in this work directory.

The specific Painter note says to record the airborne-house scale concern without another redo because a fresh attempt already occurred. Interpret this as a record-and-revalidate request: retain existing artwork, perform no new art generation or scale repair, and do not claim the concern was fixed.

Reuse thirteen selected built-in imagegen sources in original dependency order: base, idle, running-right, remaining standard rows, cardinals, look row 9, look row 10. This run makes zero image-generation calls; original creation made 17 calls including four superseded sources.
Preserve the previously accepted uniform 1.20x complete-row-10 transform. This is an inherited correction, not a new repair; never normalize poses individually.
Retain the fixed family contact reference and verify its supplied SHA-256. Preserve Warm Oilcloth Family taste, Broomstep identity, window eyes, kerchief roof, open chicken-leg gap and secured broom.
Retain independent left-facing artwork and the existing state distinctions: waiting leans outward, focused work sweeps low, review inspects the raised broom inward.
Use original alpha, bundled extraction and assembly, one final blue-key despill, then the established compact 256-color nondithered lossless WebP encoding. No source art is redrawn.
Carry forward the existing four-beat frame remaps and held-pose preview timing. Numerical motion guidance is documented, not a separate gate.
Preserve inherited prompts and generation metadata as historical records, clearly separate from the zero calls made in this run.

The rebuilt final atlas is byte-for-byte identical to the prior validated candidate: SHA-256 5e65e87c3a3b6d221388719a8f55a64ad3ef85663234f008dd0446b2426673dc. This run does not claim a visual fix to jumping row 4 frames 1–3.

Record the Painter concern: the airborne wooden house appears smaller than idle beyond bent-leg shortening. The specific instruction asks to record this without another redo; no new whole-pet or row redraw was made.

Jump target 10–14 px versus bundled measured airborne lift 35 px and landing difference 1 px. Crouch, spring, peak, landing and settle remain readable; the amplitude difference alone is not an acceptance failure.

Idle breath target 1–2 px versus observed alpha>=32 bounds with tops y=7–18 and bottoms y=199–201. Blink and gentle posture changes retain the intended calm loop. Framing guidance x=16–176,y=16–192,baseline=184 differs from bundled fitting (idle median baseline 201 and jump top 6); these observations trigger no extra numeric gate or repair.

Preview timing retains bundled holds: idle 280/110/110/140/140/320 ms; travel 120 ms, last 220; wave/jump 140 ms, last 280; failed 140 ms, last 240; waiting 150 ms, last 260; work 120 ms, last 220; review 150 ms, last 280. Look loop uses 180 ms per direction. These preserve action rhythm rather than a literal two-second 16-frame row.

All nine row extractions used connected components. Bundled preparation, per-row and full frame inspection, standard composition, cardinal extraction, sequential look registration, exactly one despill, atlas v2 validation, direction continuity and final quality validation ran successfully. One premature registration command was retried after its input existed.

Three isolated read-only reviewers passed all cardinal axes through bundled majority and blind validators. 022.5 and 045 horizontal cues remain ambiguous to the majority and warning-level in labeled review; the upward-right pupil cue remains visible. Other cardinal and intermediate axes pass.

Continuity warnings for open leg/claw gaps and difference outliers remain documented. Look widths are 128–140 px, maximum ratio 1.09375; native visual review found no new conspicuous look-row scale change.

Native visual review confirms outward waiting, low broom sweep during focused work, and inward inspection of the raised broom during review. Similar neutral endpoints remain, while the middle gestures distinguish the states.

All nine state GIFs, all-state GIF/MP4, native idle-jump-idle GIF/MP4, ordered look-loop GIF/MP4, contact sheets, direction sheet, four labeled stills and an ordered idle-jump-idle strip were rendered from the exact final WebP. Visual inspection used ordered frame sheets and stills; no timed playback capability is claimed.

No new generation or visual repair occurred. The current generation log is empty; thirteen cached original sources, their prompts, references, historical 17-call metadata and inherited deterministic transformations are retained under decoded/, sources/ and logs/.

Output is a transparent 1536×2288 v2 WebP, 714020 bytes. WebP, compressed contact sheet, metadata and full provenance together remain below 2 MB; all required reports are in qa/ and previews in previews/.

Rightward door/window cluster remains at the right while roof pitches farther forward and eyes point down-right.
Pupils lie low and right beneath the low eave; the facade bends down-right while feet remain grounded.
Both pupils sit at the bottom of the windows, with cream above; the broad roof tips forward. Clear downward cardinal.
Pupils sit low-left within the windows and the facade turns slightly screen-left; forward roof pitch supplies downward axis.
Left-facing facade exposes the right wall; lowered pupils sit under a low eave, combining down and left.
Facade and door gather toward the left; pupils remain low as the roof pitches forward. Leftward axis is dominant with a smaller down cue.

repairs: Redrew only jumping row 4, preserving house and roof mass while bending the chicken legs. No additional art retries.

contract_overrides.original: Each row has 16 frames at 8 fps: two seconds, four beats of four frames. Repeat held drawings within that grid.
contract_overrides.replacement: Rows 0–8 contain 6,8,8,4,5,8,6,6,6 frames. Remap four beats to these counts; retain 8 fps as rhythm guidance and use bundled preview holds.
contract_overrides.reason: The v2 contract fixes frame counts.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: settled pose. Beat 2: one slow blink or slight head dip. Beat 3: a 1–2 pixel breath. Beat 4: return and hold. Keep sleepy pets curled, proud pets upright and the palette quietly seated. Loop gently.
contract_overrides.replacement: 6 frames; beats map to frames 0; 1–2; 3–4; 5. Preserve settled stance, slow window blink, breath and return.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count; motion amplitudes remain guidance.

contract_overrides.original: Face right. Beat 1: first contact. Beat 2: lift and pass. Beat 3: opposite contact. Beat 4: lift and return. Legs stride, wheels turn, covers or bee wings beat; legless bodies tip and bob along the same pulse. Keep carried objects secure.
contract_overrides.replacement: 8 frames; beats map to frames 0–1; 2–3; 4–5; 6–7. Preserve right-facing alternating chicken-leg contacts and the secured broom.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count.

contract_overrides.original: Use the same four-beat travel cycle facing left. Redraw the turn so the eyebrow, herbs, quill, broom, guitar and other uneven details remain attached to their proper places. Do not simply mirror the finished sheet.
contract_overrides.replacement: 8 frames; beats map to frames 0–1; 2–3; 4–5; 6–7. Retain independent left-facing drawings and attached asymmetric details.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: turn toward the viewer. Beat 2: raise an available limb, cover, branch or body edge. Beat 3: make one clear greeting sweep. Beat 4: lower and settle. Bodies without limbs tilt in greeting. Keep held flames and jars upright. Play once.
contract_overrides.replacement: 4 frames; beats map to frames 0; 1; 2; 3. Preserve the lifted-claw greeting and stable finish.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: crouch or compress. Beat 2: rise 10–14 pixels. Beat 3: reach the peak and descend. Beat 4: land, soften and settle. Winged pets use a brief upward flap; the trolleybus gives a small springy hop. Show no trails or landing marks. Play once.
contract_overrides.replacement: 5 frames; beats map to frames 0; 1; 2; 3–4. Crouch, rise, peak, land and settle; preserve rigid house dimensions and bend the legs. The 10–14 pixel target remains drawing guidance.
contract_overrides.reason: The v2 count requires five frames; the maker instruction targets disappearing house mass.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: stop abruptly. Beat 2: sink or tilt downward. Beat 3: hold a plainly disappointed pose. Beat 4: recover slightly while keeping the lowered gaze. No damage or comic panic. Play once and hold; this must differ from a sleepy idle.
contract_overrides.replacement: 8 frames; beats map to frames 0–1; 2–3; 4–5; 6–7. Preserve folded knees, disappointed roof tilt and lowered gaze.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: look toward the expected action. Beat 2: hold. Beat 3: make one restrained questioning tilt or weight shift. Beat 4: hold with eyes open. The calf may make one small hoof press. Existing lights stay steady. Loop without pacing.
contract_overrides.replacement: 6 frames; beats map to frames 0; 1–2; 3–4; 5. Preserve outward attention, raised heel and restrained questioning tilt.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count.

contract_overrides.original: This means a task is active, not travel. Stay planted and lean toward the work. Beat 1: prepare. Beat 2: act. Beat 3: check. Beat 4: reset. The hut sweeps close to its feet, the brush works at its own jar rim, the inkpot traces an empty underline gesture, the book turns a pictured page and the magnifier scans. Other seeds use focused body motions with their existing belongings. Loop.
contract_overrides.replacement: 6 frames; beats map to frames 0; 1–2; 3–4; 5. Keep Broomstep planted while its attached broom prepares, sweeps low, pauses for checking and resets.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count while retaining focused-work semantics.

contract_overrides.original: Beat 1: become still and attentive. Beat 2: inspect an existing body detail or belonging, or turn thoughtfully when there is none. Beat 3: hold the considered pose. Beat 4: give one small nod and settle. The magnifier angles its lens inward; the palette studies a paint dab. Keep the motion small and distinct from the broad greeting. Add nothing. Play once.
contract_overrides.replacement: 6 frames; beats map to frames 0; 1–2; 3–4; 5. Preserve inward inspection of the raised existing broom, a held pose and a small settling nod.
contract_overrides.reason: Remap the four beats to the required v2 count.

contract_overrides.original: V2 adds sixteen selectable looks to the base sheet, each covering all nine rows and all twenty seeds. These change paint handling and small accents, never creature, costume or props: 1. Dry Paint—sparse broad grain; 2. Full Paint—solid matte fills; 3. Thin Paint—slightly translucent fills; 4. Broken Edge—small fixed gaps in solid-body outlines; 5. Soft Edge—gentler edge transitions; 6. Firm Edge—clearer shape boundaries; 7. Cream Edge—a narrow light-facing rim; 8. Soot Edge—a deeper inward border; 9. Ochre Touch—ochre on existing small accents; 10. Rust Touch—rust on existing small accents; 11. Herb Touch—green on existing small accents; 12. Blue Touch—blue on existing small accents; 13. Pale Paint—lighter secondary colors; 14. Deep Paint—darker secondary colors; 15. Quiet Paint—less saturated secondary colors; 16. Fresh Paint—stronger secondary colors. Protect identity colors and face contrast in every look. Glass variants affect rim softness, tint or inner light only; its center remains clear.
contract_overrides.replacement: Sixteen gaze/pose directions with unchanged palette and treatment: row 9 = 000,022.5,045,067.5,090,112.5,135,157.5; row 10 = 180,202.5,225,247.5,270,292.5,315,337.5. Clockwise screen coordinates: 000 up,090 right,180 down,270 left.
contract_overrides.reason: V2 looks are directions, not paint variants or additional animation sets.

contract_overrides.original: Place a single centered pose on a perfectly flat pure blue #0000FF chroma-key background.
contract_overrides.replacement: Use genuine transparent RGBA; retain the selected blue key only for deterministic cleanup.
contract_overrides.reason: The user requires genuine transparency.

decisions: Local-only maker attempt. No Pets MCP, Library, upload or service lifecycle calls occurred.

The current maker instruction authorizes the targeted jump repair and supersedes the earlier record-only instruction. Earlier art and rejection evidence were preserved; the Lamp outcome remains unchanged.
Reused the base, eight sound animation rows, cardinal anchors and both directional rows. Generated only one coherent five-pose jumping strip.
Retained independent left-facing drawings and the inherited uniform 1.20x complete-row-10 source correction.
Preserved the fixed family reference, Warm Oilcloth Family taste, window eyes, roof pattern and secured broom. The full corrected brief and readability guidance accompanied the image job.

Copied thirteen inherited selected sources from their recorded tool-cache paths. Preserved the replaced jump at sources/prior/jumping.png. The new source is sources/maker-jumping-01.png; prompts, references, cache paths and hashes are logged locally.
Used bundled component extraction with shared row scale, exactly one blue-key despill, and 256-color nondithered lossless WebP encoding. No individual pose resizing or procedural art.
Extracted jump widths are 149,149,149,149,147 pixels versus idle frame 0 at 153 pixels. Native ordered inspection shows substantially consistent house mass through the repaired jump.

The 10–14 pixel jump guidance compares with approximately 10 pixels of roof rise and 40 pixels of bundled foot-baseline clearance because the claws tuck underneath. Landing differs from idle by 1 pixel. These preserve the intended hop; amplitude differences were not extra gates.
Inherited idle bounds vary more than the 1–2 pixel breath guidance, with tops approximately 7–18 and bottoms 199–201. The blink and gentle posture changes remain intact.
Bundled fitting retains the inherited baseline near 201 rather than the suggested 184. Sound rows were not rescaled to enforce numeric framing guidance.
Retained bundled preview durations and one-shot holds, with four action beats remapped to v2 frame counts.

Bundled preparation, row extraction and inspection, standard assembly, cardinal extraction, sequential look registration, despill, atlas validation, continuity and pet-quality checks all completed successfully without modifying validators.

Three isolated read-only reviewers passed cardinal axes through bundled majority and blind validators. Directions 022.5 and 045 retain reviewed horizontal-ambiguity warnings; labeled inspection confirms subtle upward-right cues. Intentional leg gaps and continuity outliers remain documented warnings.
Waiting retains outward attention, focused work sweeps the broom low, and review inspects the raised broom inward. No other state was redrawn.

Rendered nine state GIFs, all-state GIF/MP4, native idle-jump-idle GIF/MP4, directional GIF/MP4, contact and direction sheets, labeled motion stills and an ordered transition strip from the exact final WebP.
Visual inspection used native ordered frames and labeled stills; no real-time video playback capability is claimed.
This run used one image-generation call and one targeted repair. Historical creation used 17 calls; the previous record-only run used zero. No whole-pet redo or further art retry occurred.
Final transparent atlas is 1536×2288 and 718710 bytes. Atlas, compressed contact, metadata and provenance total approximately 1.40 MB.
The candidate remains local. Independent caller validators and the separate image jury are still required before publication.

contract:
The v2 sprite-sheet contract fixes 192 × 208 cells, eight columns by eleven rows,
one transparent 1536 × 2288 atlas. The nine animation rows (0–8) have these exact frame counts:
idle 6, running-right 8, running-left 8, waving 4, jumping 5, failed 8, waiting 6,
running 6 (focused work, not locomotion), review 6. Unused cells stay fully transparent.
Rows 9 and 10 hold sixteen look directions, eight per row, clockwise in screen coordinates:
row 9: 000, 022.5, 045, 067.5, 090, 112.5, 135, 157.5;
row 10: 180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5.
000 is up, 090 right, 180 down, 270 left. These are gaze/pose directions with the same
palette and treatment, not sixteen palette variants, paint treatments or separate animations.
motion_policy: Style-sheet motion numbers (pixel displacement, angles, timing and amplitudes) are drawing guidance. Only the skill's validators gate a pet; a measured difference from style guidance is recorded in provenance, not a reason to fail or spend repairs.
